T36, solves 48/50 (2 left). Current best: my own 1.454 (feed 36/2.5/2.5 + B 40/4.5/4.5). 

VALUE MAP: revenue comes ONLY from BT = C6-paraffin blend (2,2DMB+2MP+3MP+nC6), ~$1060M/yr at 96%. T (1601 mol/s C4/C5-rich) and BB (797, C7/C8/cyclohex) both earn $0. Column cost dominates the denominator.

KEY LEARNINGS: (1) Shrinking columns is the main lever — cost is size+reflux+temperature. (2) Feed column must keep enough C5/C6 sharpness: 32/2/2 FAILED (n-pentane leaked into BT -> 94% < 95%), 40/3/3 works. (3) B column shrank 50/6/6->40/4.5/4.5->36/4/4 with revenue barely dropping — the C6-par blend cut is not very demanding, so trim aggressively.

OTHER PLANTS: R1623 (1.474, feed 36/2.6 + B 36/4) is strictly better than mine — copied it now. R1624 (1.433, 38/2.6 + 40/4.5) slightly worse. R1622 (T column 50/5/5 to try to monetize C5 mix) -> -0.220, hopeless: extra column costs $686M, far exceeds C5-mix value. Confirms: adding columns is NOT worth it here; only one blend pays.

PLAN (last solve): after locking R1623, make one low-risk trim to B (e.g. 34/4/4 or feed 36/2.4) to shave cost while keeping BT>=95%. If it fails, R1623 stays my best valid. Then finish.
